how_to_read.lines: Every coded CFR line for the year with the label as printed in that year's workbook. 'subtotal_lines' holds the workbook's own subtotals (I01/2, I08a/b, I18 totals of I18a-d, E28a/b), which are not added again.
how_to_read.fbit_match: true when every FBIT history-API figure for the year agrees with the workbook to within £1 (teacher FTE to within 0.05); fbit_exact says whether all were identical; fbit_differences lists each gap.
how_to_read.totals.reconciliation: Line sums minus the workbook's own totals; small non-zero values are pence rounding.

ptfa.name: WILLIAM PATTEN PARENTS TEACHERS & FRIENDS ASSOCIATION
ptfa.objects: TO ADVANCE THE EDUCATION OF PUPILS IN THE SCHOOL IN PARTICULAR BY:    (1) DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN STAFF, PARENTS AND OTHERS ASSOCIATED WITH THE SCHOOL;    (2) ENGAGING IN ACTIVITIES OR PROVIDING FACILITIES OR EQUIPMENT WHICH SUPPORT THE SCHOOL AND ADVANCE THE EDUCATION OF THE PUPILS
ptfa.area_of_benefit: NOT DEFINED BUT IN PRACTICE THE CATCHMENT AREA OF WILLIAM PATTEN SCHOOL
ptfa.activities_as_registered: We raise funds for the school to spend on educational equipment, books, trips, sports and music activities and equipment, visits and additional onsite or offsite projects delivered in conjunction with the school and external  providers. We provide funding for additional staff outside normal class times as required.We also promote communication between the school, teachers and parents.

school_website.summary: PTFA role: 'to support our amazing school with funds to facilitate a number of hugely important activities including fit for sport staff at breaks and large projects' and to bring the parent community together. Funds go towards 'music lessons, educational school trips and themed events throughout the year, such as arts, international and science days, a Christmas tree and decorations'. A 'longer-term fundraising initiative to update the Early Years playground' is being drafted. 100% volunteer-led; seeking a social media coordinator, fundraising coordinator (business donations, sponsorship for e.g. a playground refresh) and event helpers. Runs easyfundraising.

ptfa.relationship_to_school_accounts: CFR line I13 'donations and/or voluntary funds' covers money 'paid into the main school budget', including 'income from fund-raising activities' and parents' contributions (DfE CFR framework 2025 to 2026, Income section). Any PTFA money paid to the school therefore appears in the school's own income. The PTFA's treasurer letters describe it 'combin[ing] with the school to fund annual activities' and 'mealtime cover reimbursement', but the accounts do not say which payments went to the school and which straight to suppliers, and the years differ (PTFA September-August, CFR April-March), so the overlap cannot be measured. School I13 by CFR year: 2022-23 £4,275.63, 2023-24 £27,315, 2024-25 £16,894, 2025-26 £3,687.

forum_statements.statement: Overall school balances 'remained in credit at the year-end, with approximately £4 million in revenue reserves'. 'The deficits of four schools that closed last year were written off by the council, and a similar process will occur for schools closing or merging this summer.' Concern 'that the overall school balances might go into deficit in the next year or two'.

'The budget deficit stems from a faster-than-anticipated decline in student enrollment, a trend expected to continue', together with the challenges of 'smaller, unfederated schools'. Item 4: a 'more robust process' for licensed deficit agreements and cash-flow loans; deficits licensed in the interim while schools work to a sustainable budget in the medium term.
Schools with deficits include 'some exceeding a million pounds and others under £100,000'. Action: a detailed report on schools with licensed deficits to come to the Forum.

Item 3.3: the 2024-25 outturn shows 'approximately 11 schools under review'; 'a large percentage of the current £4.7 million deficit is due to two special schools'; 'tighter, more intrusive deficit agreements are necessary'.

'The primary issue discussed frequently is falling pupil numbers, which is likely to diminish the School Block.' Growth funding supports reorganisation 'following the closure of four primary schools'.
School reserves across Hackney maintained schools fell from £16,150,726 (2021-22) to £12,424,699 (2022-23), £7,446,624 (2023-24) and £4,301,534 (2024-25).
Redundancy panel criteria changed to remove the 'falling rolls' requirement, so schools in financial difficulty qualify regardless of roll.
Item 4, Final End of Year Position for Schools – School Balances 2025-26, presented for noting.

Reserve limits described as 5% (secondary) and 8% (primary); 'schools with surplus balances exceeding approximately 12% are required to submit expenditure plans'. Councillors asked for a breakdown of 'the £6m deficit of closed schools' and raised the impact of partly funded pay awards on 'schools already operating under license deficit agreements'. Officers noted 'further school closures may be necessary in the future due to declining student enrollment numbers'.

closures.statement: Hackney's Cabinet agreed on 22 April 2025 to close or merge six schools from September 2025: St Mary's CofE Primary and St Dominic's Catholic Primary closed; Oldhill Community School merged into Harrington Hill; Sir Thomas Abney merged into Holmleigh (which moved to the Sir Thomas Abney site). William Patten is not among them. Hackney snapshot: 2,400 fewer primary pupils in January 2024 than January 2017; 610 (23%) vacant reception places in October 2024.
closures.searched: All 33 Schools Forum documents on the HSFS extranet (18 sets of minutes and 15 agendas, June 2021 to July 2026) and the 24 publicly readable papers linked from the November 2025, February 2026 and July 2026 minutes (2 more returned HTTP 401) were searched for 'Patten'; the only mentions are the four in school_specific. None proposes closing or amalgamating William Patten.

scheme_for_financing_schools.version: Hackney Scheme for Financing Schools, 'Effective from April 2021' (PDF dated 6 September 2021), the version on the HSFS extranet on 2026-11-07
scheme_for_financing_schools.surplus_reporting: Governing bodies must report their intended use of surplus balances above 5% (secondary) or 8% (primary, special and PRU), with a spending plan by 31 May; surpluses should be used within three years (s4.1.1, p.25).
scheme_for_financing_schools.surplus_clawback: The LA claws back surplus 'where a school has had a combined revenue and capital surplus balance of 12% or more for three successive years (the excess above 12% being the amount clawed back)', automatic unless a dispensation is agreed (s4.2, p.26).
deficit_rules: A deficit is carried forward and set against next year's budget share; schools in deficit at 31 March must plan to recover in the following year, and deficit recovery plans are required for all schools in deficit at year end (s4.4, p.26).

Deficit budgets need the express permission of the Director of Education and the Director of Finance, and only for closure, a fall in budget share of 5% or more, or other exceptional circumstances; a recovery plan is required when the revenue deficit is above 5% at 31 March; unavoidable deficits must operate under licence, with a recovery plan agreed before the budget is set (s4.5, p.26).
A recovery plan sets out measures, pupil and budget forecasts, and a timescale to balance of no more than 3 years; withdrawal of delegation may be considered if it is not followed (p.27).
Schools pay interest on deficit balances at their bank's rate (s4.6, p.27). 'The Council cannot write-off the deficit balance of any school' (s4.7, p.27).

Licensed deficits are unlikely for sums under 2% of the school's ISB share; repayment over no more than three years (s4.9, p.28). Annex E (p.64): licences are capped at 10% of the school's ISB share and at 20% of cumulative credit balances across schools, with repayment deducted from the ISB share.
scheme_for_financing_schools.differences_from_minutes: The 1 July 2026 minutes (p.4) describe 12% as the level above which expenditure plans are required, while the 2021 Scheme makes 12% for three successive years the automatic clawback trigger and 8% (primary) the plan trigger. The 2 July 2025 minutes (p.4) say closed schools' deficits 'were written off by the council', while Scheme s4.7 says the Council cannot write off a school's deficit. A newer Scheme may exist but was not published on the extranet.

discrepancies.detail: The brief suggested LAEstab 2042128; every CFR workbook (2018-19 to 2025-26) gives LA 204, Estab 2897, LAEstab 2042897.

Pipeline total_income 3,025,090 and total_expenditure 2,991,578 vs the workbook's 3,050,253 and 3,016,741. The pipeline subtracts E30 direct revenue financing (£25,163, a revenue contribution to capital, matched by CI04 £25,163) from both, to match the 2020-21+ definition (I01:I18 - E30; E01:E29 + E31 + E32). The in-year balance (33,512) and reserve (543,908) are unchanged.
discrepancies.impact: Intentional and consistent with FBIT's current definitions; FBIT does not show 2019-20, so it cannot be checked there. Flagged as derived in the row.

discrepancies.detail: FBIT in-year balance -172,653 (2021-22) and -169,785 (2025-26) vs the workbook's -172,654 and -169,784. FBIT subtracts the rounded total expenditure from the rounded total income; the workbook works from pence.
FBIT 3,449,419 vs workbook 3,449,420; FBIT's figure equals the sum of the whole-pound lines (I01 + I03 + I05 + I06 + I07 + I18).
Teachers FTE: FBIT 23.08 (2024-25) and 23.65 (2025-26) from the school workforce census; the CFR workbooks give 23.1 and 23.6 (rounded to 1 dp). Other years agree.

In 2020-21, 2021-22, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 the whole-pound line items sum to within £3 of the workbook's own totals; the totals were computed from pence. Opening balance + in-year balance = closing reserve to within £1 in every year.

discrepancies.impact: None on the reserve; only the split between pupil-focused and community-focused balances differs.

discrepancies.detail: The pipeline uses the workbook's 'Supply Staff: E02 + E10 + E26', which includes E10 supply teacher insurance (premiums and de-delegated cover schemes): 2025-26 = 0 + 35,831 + 82,434 = 118,265 (£273 a pupil). FBIT counts supply staff as E02 + E26 = 82,434 (£191 a pupil) and puts E10 under other costs.
discrepancies.impact: The site's 'Supply staff' figure for this school is 43% higher than what FBIT calls supply staff. Similar-school medians use the same definition, so the comparison is like-for-like, but the label misleads.

discrepancies.detail: The 2024-25 workbook's 'Educational Supplies: (E19:E21)' (157,536) includes E20D administration software (£10,211); the 2025-26 column '(E19:E20C) + (E20E:E21)' excludes it, as FBIT does in both years (FBIT moves E20D into administrative supplies). On a 2025-26 basis 2024-25 would be 147,325.
discrepancies.impact: Breaks year-on-year comparison of 'Learning resources & ICT' for every school with E20D spend in 2024-25; the site's latest-year comparison (2025-26) is unaffected.

discrepancies.where: site school page, 'Money raised by parents'
discrepancies.detail: The page says 'Parent associations' money isn't in the school's accounts above.' CFR I13 includes fund-raising income and parents' contributions paid into the school budget, and the PTFA's own letters describe reimbursing the school for mealtime cover.
discrepancies.impact: The statement is wrong for any PTA money paid to the school; it should say the two can overlap and must not be added together.

discrepancies.detail: Pupils are formatted with Python's round-half-to-even: 432.5 shows as 432 and 430.5 as 430, but 427.5 shows as 428 and 437.5 as 438.

discrepancies.where: PTFA accounts y/e Aug 2023 vs annual return AR22
discrepancies.detail: Comparatives £16,400 income / £9,400 spending vs annual return £15,951 / £9,339.
Treasurer's letters quote funds including a £1,750 cash float (and exclude the lottery account), and the 2023-24 letter gives spending as £37,030 and £36.2k against £36,767 in the accounts.
Two OCR misreads were corrected using the accounts' own totals: 2024-25 SEND 1,600 (not 4,600) and 2023-24 Lunch Clubs Support 12,226 (not 42,226).
discrepancies.impact: Check both against the filed PDFs on the register.

discrepancies.detail: Every register page returned 'Sorry, there was an issue displaying this content' to a plain request. A retry with a browser-style cookie session was blocked by the agent's permission policy as bot-check circumvention and was not pursued. Income, spending, volunteers and filing dates come from the official bulk extract; trustee counts come from the filed accounts; the accounts' content comes from opencharities.uk's transcription of the filed PDFs.
discrepancies.impact: Trustee counts for 2020-21 and 2021-22 (no accounts filed) are missing; the PDFs themselves were not downloaded.
